text:
maria: deploy-bot auto-rollback kicked in for canary today at 12:16 UTC due to a p95 latency spike. I'm seeing a short-lived spike in the metrics dashboard but the traces look like sampling noise. :thinking:
deploy-bot: autopilot: detected p95 latency > 500ms for 3 minutes; initiating safe rollback to v3.9.1. Reason: latency_threshold_violation.
josh: link to grafana: https://grafana.internal/r/abc123 — looks like a burst from one host group, not global.
eve: checked kube events — we had a flurry of node eviction warnings in eu-west-1 around the same time. Not sure if it's infra-related or application.
paul: any customer-facing errors reported? Sentry shows a small bump in 5xxs but mostly timeouts, stack traces point to slow kv lookups.
maria: okay, two questions: 1) do we accept deploy-bot's rollback or pin current release and investigate? 2) what's the comms plan if we manual-rollback?
josh: my vote is to hold the rollback (cancel autopilot) for 15 mins while we validate. If it's infra noise we'll re-run canary.
eve: agree — if we cancel autopilot we should still isolate the canary traffic slice and ramp down further. Might be safe to pin the previous version for customer pools if needed.
maria: @deploy-bot can you pause further automated rollbacks for this rollout id 0x9f3c for 30m?
deploy-bot: command accepted: autopilot-paused for rollout 0x9f3c (30m). To resume: `deploy-bot resume 0x9f3c`.
paul: drafting a quick release-note blurb in case we need to notify customers: "Intermittent latency spike observed during today's canary; we have paused the rollout while we investigate. No data loss reported." Thoughts?
josh: add: "If you see degraded performance please open a ticket and mention case #RL-1245" — helps routing.
eve: ops note: set traffic-fallback to regional fallback policy (eu->us) for 10m to reduce customer impact: `rb set-fallback eu-west-1 us-west-2 --duration=10m`.
maria: good. we'll do: pause autopilot, enable fallback, collect traces, 15m re-eval. If errors persist -> manual rollback to v3.9.1 and notify customers.
paul: I'll post the customer-facing snippet to the release-notes channel and draft an internal incident blurb for Sales. Snippet: "We're pausing a phased rollout after seeing transient latency in one region. We're on it and will update in 30 minutes".
josh: ops: can you confirm whether dedicated customers on reserved pools were hit? If so, we may prefer immediate manual rollback instead of a pin.
eve: checked reserved pools: no dedicated pools hit; only host-group A (shared) had the spike.
maria: decision: cancel autopilot rollback, pin rollout (so no further traffic increases), enable fallback for 10m, collect data, manual rollback if p95 > 400ms at next check. Owners: eve (ops) for fallback+traces, josh (eng) to validate traces, paul (comms) to prepare customer note.
deploy-bot: rollout 0x9f3c pinned to v3.10.0 (pin-id: pin-844). Autopilot remains paused.
oncall-bot: oncall alert created: RL-1245 assigned to eve. Escalation window 30m.
paul: internal comms draft: "Heads up — canary paused after transient latency spike; we've pinned the rollout and enabled regional fallback while we investigate. No dedicated customers impacted. We'll share a follow-up in 30m or earlier if we roll back".
maria: thanks. if anyone sees customer impact escalate immediately and we have >1% error rate for 5m we proceed with manual rollback. Otherwise keep this pinned and we'll re-evaluate at +15m.
josh: logging my check steps: `curl -s $SRE_TRACE_API/rollouts/0x9f3c | jq .events` then `kubectl logs -l app=service -n prod --since=10m` — will paste findings in 10m.
eve: running `rb collect-traces --rollout 0x9f3c --since 15m` now.
paul: customer note posted to support draft; pinging sales in #sales-ops. :thumbsup:
maria: ok locking this thread — we'll reopen if we hit manual-rollback threshold or resume rollout. Good catch everyone!
